| Scene description | • S09-B covers pavement and roadside space on Liangdao Street Food Street, Wuchang District, Wuhan.<br>• S09-B-01: a clean other-waste/recyclables bin beside paving and railings has no overflow or accumulation, with vehicles and an information board behind.<br>• S09-B-02: black wheeled bins stand beneath a roadside shelter; the right bin overflows with green bags, while others are not full, near trees, curbs, and cones.<br>• S09-B-03: red and transparent bags, possibly food residue or packaging, accumulate on cardboard beside electric bicycles and a curb without a bin.<br>• S09-B-04: a shopfront other-waste/food-waste bin overflows in the food-waste compartment with bottles and food containers; an adjacent black wheeled bin is not full, near a pharmacy and shared bicycles.<br>• S09-B-05: a transparent bag with boxes and bottles and an open red heart-pattern fabric bag accumulate beside steps, shop windows, and a manhole, outside bins. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should be clean, intact, non-overflowing, and accessible without obstructing passage. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 15.<br>• Commercial and catering areas require sorting bins and scheduled collection against accumulation. Implementation Plan for the Municipal Solid Waste Classification System (State Council General Office Document〔2017〕26), Article 3.<br>• Casual stockpiling or dumping on roads, pavements, or public green space is prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 17.<br>• Standard containers require separate food/other-waste disposal and no mixing during collection. Signs for classification of municipal solid waste (GB/T 19095-2019).<br>• Collectors should follow agreed times and not retain overflowing waste beyond 2 hours. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 21.<br>• Businesses or managers failing bin provision or allowing overflow or accumulation require correction; continued non-compliance may incur CNY 500–5,000. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two overflows and three accumulations affect pavements and shopfronts, impairing appearance and access without severe pollution or blockage. Food residues pose sanitation risks. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: spillage and pavement accumulations obstruct access and impair appearance; food residues may breed insects and odors. Possible short-term impacts: delays may prompt complaints and vector risks; cloudy, mild weather may accelerate organic decay and local pollution. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** insufficient or unscheduled collection; S09-B-02 and S09-B-04 overflow without visible collectors. Verify schedules and that day's records.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** improper business or public disposal; fabric and transparent bags at S09-B-03 and S09-B-05 may be temporary storage or litter. Observe disposal and bin access.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** one or two bins may not meet peak catering demand at S09-B-02 and S09-B-04. Compare provision standards and generation. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, neglected sanitation areas may breed insects and odors, reduce resident and visitor satisfaction, impair urban appearance, and trigger penalties increasing compliance costs. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** empty S09-B-02 and S09-B-04, clear S09-B-03 and S09-B-05, ensure prompt designated disposal, and add temporary anti-stockpiling signs.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) add bins or collections based on generation, especially lunch and dinner peaks; (2) educate businesses and users, provide guidance, and advise or publicize violations; (3) inspect food and commercial streets daily and act promptly. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Overflow and accumulations affect sanitation and appearance in a busy food street without serious blockage or pollution. Remove within 24 hours and initiate rectification against severe escalation. |
